Ginger Thins

Served at: Lussinatta (St. Lucia's Vigil)

About 6-8 dozen cookiesPrep 30 min active + 2 hours chillingCook 6-8 min per batch

Lussinatta, the vigil of St. Lucia's Day (December 13th), marks the beginning of the Christmas season in Sweden and other Nordic countries. These crisp, spicy ginger thins, known as pepparkakor, are a beloved treat enjoyed during this festive time, often served with coffee, glögg (mulled wine), or simply as a delightful snack. Their warm spices evoke the cozy spirit of the season.

Ingredients

  • 1/2 cup (113g) unsalted butter, softened
  • 1/2 cup (100g) packed light brown sugar
  • 1/4 cup (60ml) dark molasses (or Swedish dark syrup)
  • 2 cups (240g) all-purpose flour
  • 1 teaspoon baking soda
  • 1 tablespoon ground ginger
  • 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground cloves
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground cardamom (optional)
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt

Method

  1. In a large bowl, cream together the softened butter and packed light brown sugar with an electric mixer until light and fluffy.
  2. Beat in the dark molasses until well combined.
  3. In a separate medium bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour, baking soda, ground ginger, ground cinnamon, ground cloves, ground cardamom (if using), and salt.
  4. Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients, mixing on low speed until just combined and a soft dough forms. Do not overmix.
  5. Divide the dough into two equal portions. Shape each portion into a flat disk, wrap tightly in plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or preferably overnight, to allow the flavors to meld and the dough to firm up.
  6. Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C). Line several baking sheets with parchment paper.
  7. On a lightly floured surface or between two sheets of parchment paper, roll out one disk of chilled dough very thinly, about 1/16 to 1/8 inch (1.5-3mm) thick. The thinner the dough, the crispier the cookies will be.
  8. Using cookie cutters of your choice (traditional shapes include stars, hearts, or simple rounds), cut out the ginger thins. Carefully transfer them to the prepared baking sheets, leaving about 1 inch (2.5 cm) between cookies.
  9. Bake for 6-8 minutes, or until the edges are lightly browned and the cookies are firm. Baking time may vary depending on thickness and oven.
  10. Let the cookies cool on the baking sheets for a few minutes before transferring them to a wire rack to cool completely. Repeat with the remaining dough, gathering and re-rolling scraps as needed.

Tips

  • For extra thin and crispy cookies, roll the dough directly between two sheets of parchment paper. This prevents sticking and makes transfer easier.
  • These ginger thins are delicious on their own, but also pair wonderfully with a cup of coffee, tea, or a glass of traditional Swedish glögg.
  • Store cooled ginger thins in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 weeks to maintain their crispness.
